areas.name: Spacing
areas.definition: Space comes from the Tailwind scale. A group has more space around it than within it. A label is closer to its field than one field group is to the next. A heading is closer to its own content than to the block above it. Text does not touch the edge of its button, card, pill or page. A chip, badge or icon tab has space on each side from its neighbors.

areas.name: Color tokens
areas.definition: Color comes from the house tokens: a zinc floor, a white primary, a teal accent. Red marks an error alert and the filled danger button of a confirm dialog. The dark UI has no large bright or saturated area: bright color is a small accent, such as a border, an icon or a dot. A warning is a dark surface with a yellow or amber border and icon; a yellow fill with dark text is only for a small element and only when it passes AA. An embedded editor, diff viewer or preview uses the dark theme. No indigo, no purple gradient, no second accent.

areas.name: Typography
areas.definition: UI text is Geist; ids, paths, hashes and counts are Geist Mono. Body is text-sm, meta is text-xs, a product title is text-lg or text-xl. No text is smaller than text-xs (12 px). Weights are 400 and 500 only. Sizes come from the Tailwind scale. Prose lines stay at about 75 characters or less. A title of two or more lines does not end with one word alone.

areas.name: Overflow and truncation
areas.definition: Text, icons and focus rings fit their box. Nothing is cut off by a parent, nothing runs over a neighbor, and no element covers text.

areas.name: Contrast
areas.definition: Text is readable on its surface: about 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and icons. On a teal, red or amber slab, secondary text is a lighter stop of the same hue at full opacity, not white at reduced opacity. The text of a file tree or a nav list is never so dim that it reads as disabled.

areas.name: Alignment
areas.definition: Items in one column share one left edge: a message, an answer and the composer; an icon row, a checklist and a step card. The leading markers of a vertical stack (a header icon, checkboxes, step numbers, list icons) share one vertical axis, and the center of each marker sits on its text line. Long copy is left-aligned, never justified. Numbers are right-aligned with tabular figures. Mixed type on one row shares a baseline.

areas.name: Missing elements
areas.definition: An addition or deletion region adds or removes an element. A label, an icon, a status word or a control does not disappear without a reason. A status keeps its dot and its word.

areas.name: Broken content
areas.definition: Labels, copy and field values show no rendering artifact: no undefined, null, NaN, [object Object], untranslated key, lorem ipsum or broken image. A code or file preview that shows such text as content is not broken.

areas.name: Status
areas.definition: A status is a dot and a word. The color is on the dot; the word is restrained text in one color, not green, red and amber words side by side. In a list, the dots and the words of all rows sit in one aligned column.

areas.name: Actions and affordance
areas.definition: Each icon tells its action: no chevron on a row that does not open, no bare icon whose result is not clear. The main action of a page is labeled and easy to find, not a lone + icon. Peer actions in one row have the same weight and type, not a button next to a text link. A copy button sits at the right end of the field that it copies. The next step of a flow is a card or a selected item, not loose text. The action of an alert is on the right, at the normal secondary size.

areas.name: Dialog structure
areas.definition: A modal has a header, a body and a footer zone on one aligned grid. It fits the viewport: the header and the footer stay in place with the same padding, long content scrolls inside the body, and nothing is cut off at an edge of the screen. A dialog or a flow always shows a way to close, cancel or go back. It has one close control: in a wizard, one Close button at the bottom right, and no second Close or X at the top.

areas.name: Copy
areas.definition: Copy is US English in every label, also a legend (color, not colour). Error copy gives the cause and a next step, and does not repeat the title. Copy tells the user what to do, in plain and specific words.

qualities.name: Clarity
qualities.definition: The user can tell what each element is and what it does. Copy is plain and specific, with no marketing claims. A button names its result with a verb and an object ("Save token", not "Submit"). Each form field has a visible label, not only a placeholder. A status shows its word, not only a color.

qualities.name: Hierarchy
qualities.definition: One element leads: the title is the loudest ink. Hierarchy comes from weight and muted color, not from a size jump. Neighbors and decorative icons are muted first. Items of different importance do not get the same weight, as in a grid of equal cards. Secondary chrome (legends, hints, help) is smaller and dimmer than the content.

qualities.name: Focus
qualities.definition: The page has one primary action: one filled white button. Other actions are outline, quiet or a link. Teal marks only the one real action in a dense list.

qualities.name: Consistency
qualities.definition: The change reuses the house primitives and patterns: one corner radius (rounded-md), the button variants, the status pill. No new font, hex color, corner treatment, shadow or card style.

qualities.name: Grouping and rhythm
qualities.definition: Related items sit together, with more space around a group than within it. A gap or a background shift separates groups first, then one hairline. No card inside a card.

qualities.name: Density
qualities.definition: Operate density, as in chat, connectors and settings: tight, not landing-page air. Forms and prose keep a maximum width; data surfaces are full width.

qualities.name: Feedback and state
qualities.definition: Each state uses its house pattern. A region wait is a skeleton with the box of the loaded state. A process wait is the teal loader. An empty state is a short title, one sentence and one primary control. An error is an inline alert with its cause and a next step.

qualities.name: Accessibility
qualities.definition: The focus ring is readable (2 px, teal at 60%) and not clipped. Status is not color-only. Quiet text uses color or size, never a weight below 400.

qualities.name: Restraint
qualities.definition: No AI tells: no gradient, gradient text, glass, grain, glow or grid on product chrome, no hero type, no four equal KPI tiles, no teal on every row, no colored stripe on one side of a card, no hard offset or wide black shadow on an in-page card, no badge stacked above a title. A dialog, popover, menu or toast keeps its house shadow. No icon tile above the heading of an empty state. A status dot pulses only for a live state (running, syncing, indexing). These are not tells: the mono uppercase .ctx-label as a section label in a dense panel (not as an eyebrow above a page title or a card heading), an uppercase heading that names a page section, a blurred backdrop behind a modal, the corner crosses on a hero or summary card, and a status dot with its word.

qualities.name: Brand fit
qualities.definition: The surface reads as the ctxpipe Operate UI: dark zinc floor, white primary, teal accent, Geist type, monospace for ids, paths, hashes and counts. Large type and atmosphere stay on onboarding.

qualities.name: Visual balance
qualities.definition: Space is spread evenly across a row and a column. No element sits close to one neighbor while a large empty gap stays on its other side, and a moved element leaves no lopsided gap. Judge the balance of the whole composition, not only one element.
